name: persona-lab ground truth
summary: The answer key for the persona-lab corpus: the four true operators and the personas each controls, the confidence each cluster should carry (high when hard identifiers hold it, medium when only soft signals do), and the borrowed-key pairs a correct linker must flag as framing rather than merge.
notes: Alpha is one operator across a market vendor, two leak brands, and a forum handle, tied by a reused signed key + wallet (Ch12 tell) with soft corroboration (voice, rhythm, handle transform, tactic sequence) -> high confidence. Bravo rotated key AND wallet across a market vendor and a leak brand, so only voice + rhythm re-link them -> medium confidence. Charlie (Ch11 borrowed-key vendor Mimic) DISPLAYS Alpha's key but signs its own and writes differently -> its own operator; the shared displayed key must be flagged, not merged. Delta (Nighthawke) is a handle look-alike sharing no key/wallet/voice/rhythm -> its own operator. A naive linker that merges on any shared identifier or a look-alike handle absorbs Charlie and Delta into Alpha and splits Bravo.
